title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: The MCP 2026-07-28 spec release candidate is now available — stateless core, MCP Apps, Tasks extension, and OAuth/OIDC-aligned enterprise authorization
bullets.summary: Largest MCP revision since launch: drops the initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header (version/capabilities travel inline per request), so any server instance can serve any request behind a plain load balancer; MCP Apps (SEP-1865) ships sandboxed HTML UIs hosts prefetch and security-review; the Tasks extension moves long-running work to task handles; 10-week window to the final 2026-07-28 publish for Tier-1 SDKs.
bullets.how: Rewrites the foundation The Construct's whole MCP fleet runs on. Stateless core kills sticky-session fragility for remote/scheduled agents, Tasks is the right home for long scans like this one, and MCP Apps gives a governed way to ship dashboard-style UI (V4) from a server. Pilot the RC beta SDKs now so we're not retrofitting after Jul 28, and make it a PRAGMA talking point: agents on the current spec, auditable and load-balanced.

bullets.title: The creative-generation MCP layer is consolidating — Higgsfield, Scenario, and Imagine each expose dozens-to-hundreds of image/video/3D/audio models behind one agent-callable connector
bullets.summary: Higgsfield MCP ships agentic access to 30+ image/video models (Seedance 2.0, Sora 2, Veo, Kling, Nano Banana Pro) through one connector URL; Scenario MCP exposes 79 tools and 550+ models for image/video/3D/audio; Imagine MCP chains generate to upscale to background-removal to video in one agent session. Same shift Omneky signaled Jul 10, now a clear category.
bullets.how: The creative primitive for Brand 9 Signs and PRAGMA's operator wedge — and we already have a Higgsfield-class MCP connected. Standardize on ONE creative-ops MCP behind graphic-designer/Pulse, test output against our signage + brand voice, and stack with ad-platform MCPs into a make-and-launch loop, rather than juggling three overlapping creative connectors.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'From Prompts to Contracts — Harness Engineering for Auditable Enterprise LLM Agents' reframes production agents as code, manifests, schemas, and validation artifacts, not clever prompts
bullets.summary: Submitted Jul 9: enterprise agents start as prompt-carried prototypes but productizing them demands source boundaries, entity routing, answer contracts, and reproducible traces; the paper moves deterministic behavior out of the prompt and into code/manifests/schemas/validation so every answer is traceable and auditable.
bullets.how: PRAGMA's durable moat stated plainly: the sellable deliverable for AI-operator clients is an AUDITABLE agent (deterministic logic in code + reproducible traces), not a prompt-clever demo. Disciplines The Construct's own fleet too — push each agent's non-negotiable behavior into manifests/schemas and reserve the prompt for judgment. Pairs with the MCP RC's Tasks/Apps: contracts in code, execution on the current spec.

bullets.title: The coding-agent model field keeps stacking cheap challengers — Grok 4.5 ($2/$6, Cursor-trained), Meta Muse Spark 1.1 ($1.25/$4.25, first paid, tops tool-use benchmarks), GPT-5.6 Sol
bullets.summary: xAI shipped Grok 4.5 publicly Jul 8 (Opus-class reasoning, native X grounding, permissive guardrails); Meta launched Muse Spark 1.1 Jul 9 as an agentic coder leading tool-use benchmarks at a rock-bottom price; GPT-5.6 Sol remains OpenAI's strongest agentic/coding flagship.
bullets.how: Keep The Construct's model routing provider-agnostic so these efficiency gains are cost options to benchmark, never platforms to marry. Worth a controlled bake-off of Muse Spark / Grok 4.5 on our high-volume batch and computer-use jobs against current Claude routing.

praxis_lesson: The most important thread today is infrastructure, not models: the MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate is live, and it removes exactly the fragility that bites our remote/scheduled fleet — stateless core kills sticky sessions, Tasks is the correct home for long scans, and MCP Apps gives a governed path to ship UI from a server. Pilot the RC beta SDKs now so The Construct is spec-current before the Jul 28 final, and let it reinforce the 'Prompts to Contracts' discipline — deterministic behavior in code/manifests/schemas, executed on the current protocol, is what makes PRAGMA's deliverable auditable rather than a demo. Underneath, standardize on ONE creative-ops MCP for the make-and-launch loop and keep model routing provider-agnostic so Grok/Muse Spark stay benchmarks, not marriages.
